o1.biggest_strength: Builds the plan on the real signals: the nurse and server Spark Ads from day 1, problem-first hooks, mission as the closer, no discount, and a day-30 check that also asks whether we own winning creative before the March licences end.
o1.biggest_mistake: The day-30 new-customer test is a before-and-after against the prior 30 days with an unexplained 70% threshold, which is exactly the kind of pre/post read that flatters a Q4 launch, and it passes a days 15-30 cost bar while quoting a 30-day order count, so the pass line doesn't line up.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Replace the prior-30-day comparison with a seasonally adjusted or holdout read, exclude existing customers from targeting, and make the day-30 cost and order-count rows use the same date window.

o2.biggest_strength: Every rule traces to money and the store's own data: $27.10 first-order profit, $38.46 90-day payback, hook costs to the cent, the 13x and 7x median-view multiples, the 32% share-of-spend benchmark for the survey, and a two-of-three reads verdict that adjusts lift for last year's seasonal jump.
o2.biggest_mistake: It commits to dated weeks around Thanksgiving without that date being in the brief, so the team could be testing a brand-new channel with unproven tracking in the most expensive week of the year, and the comment moderation and community staffing never gets an owner.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add the launch date to the 'to confirm' list with a fallback start, and give the social lead a daily comment and paid-partnership label check so the Spark Ads don't sit unattended.

reason: Both are strong and both get the money right, but Output 2 is the one I'd hand over on Monday: dated set-up tasks with owners and a 'tracking fail means no launch' gate, learning-phase maths that explains four ad groups rather than eight thin ones, and a day-30 verdict built on three reads rather than a pre/post comparison I couldn't defend to my own team.
